briefs.source_chain: Equity sell-off (AI trade hit hard after earnings, NDX worst session since June) therefore drove risk-off rates/credit (steeper curve, wider credit, rate-paying flow partly fast-money-driven) therefore a weaker Dollar except EUR, with JPY gaining as a risk-off hedge.
briefs.brief_chain: Equity sell-off (AI trade hit hard after earnings) therefore drove a choppy, steeper-curve rates session with real-money paying rate and wider credit therefore a weaker Dollar except EUR, with JPY's risk-off gains underscoring its hedge value.

distortions.what: Brief attributes the rate-paying flow to 'real money', but the source's shorthand is 'FM' ('We saw better paying of rate from FM'), the standard desk term for fast money (hedge funds/leveraged accounts), the near-opposite of real money (asset managers/pensions).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes - fast-money paying reads as a speculative, flow-driven signal, while real-money paying implies a stickier, higher-conviction institutional view; the two carry different conviction about how durable the rates move is.

distortions.what: Drops the source's AI CDS detail ('AI cds closed anywhere from +2-10bps wider') under the TMT-underperformance line.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No - the directional call (TMT underperformance on hyperscaler/AI weakness) is unchanged; this is a dropped supporting figure.

briefs.brief_chain: AI-exposure selling (Semis -8% Friday, NDX -7% in October) therefore hedge funds covered shorts (first net buy in 4 weeks) while staying net sold on Info Tech MTD and de-grossing Financials fastest in 6 months therefore a vol-crush reversal pushed flows to catch the bear thesis as S&P broke its CTA threshold, and a further break would flip GS systematic momentum negative, halting CTA buying.

distortions.what: Brief presents 'a further break would flip GS systematic momentum negative, halting CTA buying' as a continuation of the S&P CTA-threshold break just described. The source attaches that forward-looking momentum-flip warning specifically to Russell 2000 ('Should Friday's price action persist, GS systematic momentum thresholds are set to flip negative, halting projected CTA buying'), in the Futures/Russell 2K section, separate from the S&P threshold break reported in the Derivatives section.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes - the instrument at risk of the next systematic-selling trigger is Russell 2000, not the S&P 500; acting on the brief would have a trader watching/sizing the wrong index for that catalyst.

distortions.what: Brief states crude is 'down 3-3.5% on reports Trump will give Iran diplomacy more time' as a plain news-driven move. The source explicitly calls it 'optically lower' and explains 'part of the move reflects the front month rolling from Dec26 to Jan27' - i.e., part of the printed decline is a contract-roll artifact, not a real reaction to the news.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes - a trader reading the brief would overstate how much of crude's move is a genuine reaction to the Iran-diplomacy headline, since part of the figure is mechanical (contract roll) rather than news-driven.
